full_judgment: 25. It appears from the record that appellant No. 1 Fulu Mohammad filed a suit for permanent injunction against Barmans including the informant and deceased Nirendra and others as long as in 1982. The suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 20.5.86. The decree was signed on 5.6.86. The defendants took the certified copy of the judgment and decree on 23.7.86. Thereafter occurrence took place on 8.9.86. It is likely that even after losing the suit for permanent injunction Fulu Mohammad would try to retain his possession as he must have been advised by his lawyer that he had still a case in the civil Court to agitate his title to the disputed plot and it is also likely that if Barmans had not possession in the disputed land, they would try to take possession thereof soon after the dismissal of the suit. And it happened so in this case. We, therefore, hold that the accuseds were in possession of the disputed plot prior to and admittedly on the date of occurrence and the informant party entered into the disputed plot and started the assault first.
